# AAPL — Quantitative Fundamental Report
**Decision date: 2026-05-29 | Latest filing: 2026-03-28 (Q2 FY2026)**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings & Margin Trajectory

Apple's fiscal Q2 (Jan–Mar 2026) delivered revenue of $111.18B, a **+16.6% YoY** gain versus $95.36B in the year-ago quarter. This is the strongest YoY top-line growth across the five available quarters. EPS diluted reached $2.01, up **+21.8% YoY** from $1.65, and net income grew **+19.4%** to $29.58B. The QoQ declines (revenue −22.7%, EPS −29.2%) are mechanical: Q1 is the holiday quarter ($143.76B revenue, $2.84 EPS), and the seasonal step-down is consistent with prior-year patterns (Q1 FY25 $124.30B → Q2 FY25 $95.36B, a −23.3% drop).

**Margins are expanding.** Gross profit margin in Q2 FY2026 was 49.3% ($54.78B / $111.18B), up from 47.1% ($44.87B / $95.36B) a year earlier — a ~220 bps improvement. Operating income of $35.88B yields a 32.3% operating margin, compared to 31.0% in Q2 FY25 ($29.59B / $95.36B). The ratios panel confirms the trailing net margin has stepped up to 27.2% (latest) from 24.3% a year ago. This margin expansion is the clearest fundamental positive — it is not just revenue growth but improving unit economics.

## 2. Cash Generation & Balance-Sheet Resilience

Operating cash flow in Q2 FY2026 was $28.70B, **+19.8% YoY** (vs. $23.95B). The prior Q1 produced $53.92B, consistent with holiday-quarter cash collection strength. Free cash flow is unavailable in this data set, but the operating cash-flow trajectory is healthy and growing in line with earnings — no quality red flag there.

The balance sheet is materially improving. Total equity surged to **$106.49B** from $66.76B just four quarters prior (Q1 FY25), a 60% increase, while total debt declined from $94.80B to **$82.70B** over the same period. Debt-to-equity improved to **0.777** from 1.42 a year ago. Total assets stand at $371.08B. The deleveraging is real and rapid, driven by a combination of retained earnings growth and likely continued aggressive share repurchases that paradoxically inflate ROE (reported at 1.151, i.e., 115.1%) by shrinking the equity denominator faster than net income grows. This high ROE is a feature of Apple's capital-return program, not an indicator of runaway profitability — earnings power is better judged by the margin and EPS trajectories above.

## 3. Valuation vs. Own History

At **37.5x PE** (diluted, trailing), Apple sits roughly in the middle of its 365-day range of 30.3x–43.1x. Over the sparse 12-point history, the PE compressed from ~41.9x in Dec 2025 to ~31.6x in Mar 2026 before re-expanding to the current level. Price-to-book at **43.2x** is near the low end of its 38.3–65.0 range, reflecting the equity base growth. Price-to-sales is **10.2x**. The earnings yield of **2.7%** is the critical number: it sits **175 bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%** and roughly 330 bps below Moody's Baa corporate bond yield of 6.02%. A negative equity risk premium on a mature, large-cap technology company with mid-teens growth is a stretch by historical norms. The market is pricing in not just the current earnings trajectory but continued expansion and durability well beyond what the trailing numbers support.

## 4. Price Context

The stock closed at **$312.51** on 2026-05-28, within pennies of its 365-day high of $313.26. The quarterly return is **+14.5%** (from $272.95 on 2026-02-26). The 365-day low was $195.07 — the stock has rallied ~60% off that trough. Price has re-rated roughly in lockstep with the earnings beat trajectory, so the fundamental improvement is already discounted. There is no obvious "price vs. fundamentals" dislocation in either direction: the market has correctly identified the growth, and is paying a premium multiple for it.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

The macro backdrop is mixed-to-cautionary for a name trading at this valuation. The 10-year Treasury yield has risen **+40 bps** over the past ~63 trading days to 4.45%, directly compressing the relative attractiveness of a 2.7% earnings yield. The 2-year yield has climbed to 3.99% (+52 bps). The yield curve (T10Y2Y) at 0.46% remains positive but narrow. Oil has surged **+30%** to $92.65/bbl — a potential input-cost headwind for hardware margins, though Apple's current margin expansion data does not yet show this flowing through. VIX has collapsed from ~31 to **15.74**, indicating complacency and compressed risk premia — an environment that typically favors premium multiples but leaves less cushion for disappointments. The Fed Funds rate is essentially flat at 3.63%.

News sentiment is moderately positive (mean score **0.236** over 90 days, 508 articles). It has been consistently in mildly positive territory with no sustained negative streaks. This is a mood thermometer reading "comfortable" — it does not alter the fundamental view.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** The YoY margin expansion (+220 bps gross margin) combined with double-digit revenue growth (+16.6%) and declining leverage (D/E from 1.42 to 0.78 in one year) represent genuine fundamental improvement. If margins continue expanding and the revenue trajectory holds, current earnings power understates forward potential.

**Downside:** The 2.7% earnings yield versus 4.45% risk-free rate is the most exposed valuation metric. A single quarter of growth deceleration or margin compression could trigger a sharp multiple contraction from 37.5x toward the 30x floor of the recent range — a ~20% drawdown with no change in absolute earnings. The elevated oil price ($92.65) is an unpriced margin risk for hardware. Additionally, the incomplete TTM data prevents a full-year cash-flow or earnings assessment — the strongest quarter (Q4 FY25, Jul–Sep 2025) is missing from the available window, so the YoY comps may flatter if that quarter was weak.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

Apple's business fundamentals are genuinely strong: double-digit revenue and earnings growth, expanding margins, robust cash generation, and a rapidly improving balance sheet. However, the market has already priced these improvements aggressively — a 37.5x PE yielding 2.7% against a 4.45% risk-free rate leaves no margin of safety. The stock is fairly valued relative to its own recent history (mid-range PE) but expensive on an absolute basis given the rate environment. **Fundamental attractiveness is neutral: the business trajectory is healthy, but the valuation fully reflects it, offering no quantitative edge.**

qualitative_report:
# Qualitative Assessment: Apple Inc. (AAPL)
**Decision date: 2026-05-29**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Apple's franchise quality remains exceptional. The company operates a tightly integrated ecosystem spanning hardware (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Wearables), software platforms (iOS, macOS), and a rapidly scaling Services segment (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare, Apple TV+). The structural moat rests on three reinforcing pillars: (a) a 2.35+ billion active device installed base that creates powerful lock-in and cross-sell economics; (b) custom silicon (M-series, A-series) that delivers performance-per-watt advantages competitors cannot replicate without vertically integrating; and (c) privacy-first positioning that differentiates Apple from Android-based rivals.

The Services segment is the franchise's growth engine and margin engine. Services gross margin hit ~76.7% in Q2 FY2026 versus ~38.7% for Products. Services revenue reached $30.98 billion in Q2 FY2026 (a record), growing 16% year-over-year, and totaled ~$109 billion for FY2025. Structural web_search confirms the Services gross margin spread is the core driver of blended margin expansion: the segment with ~75–77% margins is growing faster than the segment with ~38–39% margins, pulling the group average upward structurally rather than cyclically.

Competitive position is strong but not unassailable. Apple holds ~20% global smartphone market share (second to Samsung at ~22% per Omdia Q1 2026), but dominates the premium segment above $600 and captures a disproportionate share of industry profit. In the U.S., iPhone commands ~58% smartphone OS share. Retention rates are quoted at ~85–92%, and Piper Sandler's spring 2025 teen survey showed 88% owning iPhones. The 92% retention figure and ecosystem depth make meaningful share erosion unlikely absent a structural platform shift.

Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly and disciplined. Apple authorized an additional $100 billion share repurchase and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.27/share effective Q3 2026. Six-month operating cash flow rose 53% year-over-year to $82.6 billion; dividend payout ratio is below 10% of OFCF. The company retired its net-cash-neutral target, instead evaluating cash ($46B) and debt ($85B) independently while maintaining $147B in total liquidity and a $62B net cash position. This is a self-sustaining capital-return machine.

The leadership transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus (announced April 20, 2026) is a first-in-15-years event. Ternus is a 25-year Apple veteran who led hardware engineering on iPhone, M-series Macs, AirPods, and Vision Pro. The market reaction has been calm, suggesting confidence in continuity, but this is an untested CEO inheriting a three-front regulatory battle and AI catch-up challenge.

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

- **Q2 FY2026 earnings (Apr 30, 2026):** Revenue $111.2B (+17% YoY), EPS $2.01 (+22% YoY), both March-quarter records. Services $30.98B (+16% YoY, record). Gross margin expanded to 49.3%. Management guided Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 14–17% YoY, well above prior expectations of ~9%.

- **$100B buyback + dividend increase (Apr 30, 2026):** New repurchase authorization and dividend raised from $0.26 to $0.27/share. $36B deployed toward repurchases in H1 FY2026.

- **Leadership transition (Apr 20, 2026):** Tim Cook stepping aside for John Ternus as CEO. Cook moves to executive chairman with a policymaker-engagement brief.

- **Supreme Court App Store ruling (Apr 6, 2026):** Court rejected Apple's appeal, requiring external payment links in apps. Potential annual commission revenue impact estimated at $2–4 billion. Combined with EU DMA (€500M fine) and DOJ antitrust suit, Apple faces a three-front regulatory challenge.

- **China rebound (Q2 FY2026):** Greater China revenue rose 28% to $20.5 billion, a notable acceleration, even as Huawei continues to compete aggressively with advanced chips.

- **India supply-chain pivot (structural):** India now accounts for ~25% of global iPhone production (up from <5% four years ago). Apple targets majority of US-bound iPhone production from India by end of 2026, partially offsetting cumulative tariff costs of $3.3 billion.

- **Tim Cook's China delegation (May 18, 2026):** Cook participated in a Trump administration trip to Beijing, signaling potential easing of tariffs and improved US-China relations that could benefit Apple's manufacturing and market access.

- **Services valuation thesis (May 19, 2026):** Evercore ISI argues Services could add $13/share if valued as a standalone high-margin software business rather than embedded in Apple's hardware multiple. Multiple firms have raised price targets above $300; Wedbush set $400.

## 3. Material Qualitative Risks and Offsets

**Risk — Three-front regulatory war.** The Supreme Court App Store ruling (Apr 6), EU DMA enforcement (€500M fine), and DOJ antitrust suit converge to structurally compress App Store commission revenue. If external payment links become standard globally, Services margins could erode by an estimated $2–4B annually. *Offset:* Services ex-App Store (iCloud, AppleCare, Apple Music, Apple Pay, advertising) are growing 12–15% organically at 70%+ margins, and Apple's privacy positioning aligns with global data-protection trends. The moat is being tested on one revenue dimension, not the entire ecosystem.

**Risk — Tariff and geopolitical exposure.** Cumulative tariff costs of $3.3B; new 10–15% blanket tariffs under Section 122 could add $100–$350 to iPhone 17 retail prices. Supply chain remains heavily concentrated in China for components. *Offset:* India manufacturing diversification is advancing rapidly (25% of iPhone production), and Cook's China visit (May 18) signals diplomatic progress. Tariff costs are material but manageable at Apple's margin and scale.

**Risk — AI catch-up.** Apple Intelligence has been criticized as "significantly lagging" competitors. Siri's major upgrade was delayed to spring 2026 due to "significant engineering problems." *Offset:* On-device AI tied to Apple Silicon could become a meaningful differentiator once shipped, and the installed base of 2.35B devices provides a distribution advantage no competitor matches. However, this remains an execution risk, not yet a realized advantage.

**Risk — Leadership transition execution.** First CEO change in 15 years during a period of regulatory war, AI competition, and supply-chain restructuring. *Offset:* Ternus's deep hardware/product pedigree and Cook's continued involvement as executive chairman provide continuity. Market reaction has been benign.

**Risk — Valuation and concentration.** Stock trades at ~36x P/E. Apple represents ~7% of the S&P 500. Analysts warn the market rally is concentrated in mega-cap tech, creating correction risk if AI expectations disappoint. *Offset:* Strong cash generation, $100B+ buyback, and accelerating revenue growth (14–17% guidance) support the multiple.

**Risk — China competitive dynamics.** Huawei's resurgence with advanced chips and local competitors marketing AI features Apple lacks in the region. Beijing's strict AI regulations require government approval for LLM commercial use, adding complexity. *Offset:* Q2 FY2026 Greater China revenue grew 28%, showing current demand resilience despite competitive pressure.

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive.** Apple's franchise quality is among the highest in global equities: an ecosystem with 2.35B+ active devices, 92% retention, a Services segment growing 16% at ~77% gross margins, custom silicon advantages, and a capital-return program returning >$100B annually. Q2 FY2026 results (17% revenue growth, 22% EPS growth, record Services) confirm the structural thesis is intact. The leadership transition appears orderly, and the dual-pronged hardware strategy (premium pricing + affordable entry points like iPhone 17e) is expanding the installed base for Services monetization.

The narrative challenges center on regulatory headwinds compressing App Store economics, AI execution lag, and tariff/geopolitical risk — all material but none existential to the core franchise. The Services business ex-regulatory-risk continues to grow double-digits at software margins, and the installed-base flywheel is self-reinforcing. Recent earnings acceleration and capital-return discipline support fundamental attractiveness, while the leadership transition and regulatory battles introduce execution uncertainty that warrants monitoring but does not negate the franchise thesis.
